contrā-versus , a, um, Part. [verto] (post-class.),
I.turned opposite, lying over against; with dat.: “Africa promontorio Apollinis Sardiniae,” Sol. 27 : “spiranti Zephy. ro contraversa (urbs) Gumathenam contingit,” Amm. 18, 9, 2 .—Adv.: contrāver-sum , on the contrary, on the other hand, = contra, Sol. 10.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
